nghi_van.mo_ta: In the street background there is a boxy, enclosed vehicle with a flat roof and square glass windows. It looks like an early 20th-century motor car or taxi, with a horse-drawn cart beside it.
nghi_van.ly_do: Motor vehicles did not exist in 1667. Coaches of the period were rounded, hung on leather straps, and had no flat roof or large square glass panes.

tra_loi.vat: A boxy, enclosed motor car (early-1900s style) standing in the street behind a woman and a horse
tra_loi.dac_diem: Square, upright cabin with a flat white-topped roof. Two small windows at the front or rear. Dark body. It looks like a Model T-era automobile. A horse and several people in long dresses and caps stand around it. Tall brick buildings line the street.
tra_loi.ly_do: The enclosed, box-bodied automobile appears to be an early-20th-century design (Model T era, about 1908–1920s). Motor cars did not exist in 1667, so it is an anachronism. Horse-drawn coaches were the only vehicles of that kind then.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The mason at lower right wears a soft flat cap with a stitched crown and short peak. He also wears a tailored grey waistcoat and a rolled-sleeve shirt, in a Victorian style.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The flat cap is a 19th-century style of working-class headgear. In 1667 London workmen wore knitted or felt caps, or broad-brimmed hats.
